text:
maya: FYI rolling a small cap change to /v1/generate hosted tier in 10m, canary 1% traffic. Goal: reduce burst-induced token cost. Please monitor 429s, p95 latency, and any auth/billing anomalies.

maya: Canary config attached: 
```
route: /v1/generate
canary_percent: 1
new_rate_limit: 120r/s per account
fallback: compatible-lite-model
rollback_triggers:
  - 5xx_rate > 0.5% for 5m
  - 429_rate > 1% for 3m
  - p95_latency increase > 40% for 5m
```

derek: got it. tagging eng-platform and eng-sre. who owns rollback if triggers fire? also include metric queries we should watch.

maya: eng-sre owns automated rollback, ops manual override if needed. watch these queries: 
- 429 rate: query(metrics.histogram, filter=route=="/v1/generate", status==429)
- p95 latency: query(metrics.latency_p95, filter=route=="/v1/generate")
- billing spike: sum(cost.tokens) by account last5m

deploy-bot: Canary start confirmed for 1% traffic (id=canary-2245). Started at 2245001240.

sophie: seeing a tiny blip on 429s from a single corporate customer at ~2245001255, spike to 0.8% but only for 30s. correlating with their burst pattern. adding logs.

leon: copy. can you share a repro curl if we need to exercise? also check auth headers — we've had header parse regressions in the last rate push.

maya: repro curl I used: 
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TEST_TOKEN' \n  -H 'X-Request-ID: test-burst-123' \n  -d '{"model":"gpt-medium","prompt":"hello","max_tokens":256}'
```
I've asked customer to share their X-Client-ID; they're sending bursts of 200 concurrent reqs in short windows.

sophie: digging logs: short excerpt: 
```
[2245001255] req_id=abc123 status=429 route=/v1/generate account=acme-corp quota_remaining=0
[2245001256] req_id=abc124 status=200 route=/v1/generate account=other-corp
```
Looks like quota exhaustion for that account at canary rate. not a platform bug yet.

derek: good catch. are the canary rate limits per-account or global? config said per account but we should confirm enforcement path. if per-account, canary interacting with customer-specific quota could surface 429s even if platform healthy.

maya: confirmed: new_rate_limit is enforced per account via quota-service v3. however the canary routing currently only applies traffic sampling, not quota scaling. so per-account quotas still apply.

leon: that means visible 429s are expected for aggressive customers. propose we hold the canary at 1% and add a short-lived exception rule: exempt known accounts from rate cut for 15m while we communicate. Thoughts?

derek: +1. prefer not to change canary %, add account whitelist for the first 30m to avoid customer impact. label it temporary and auditable.

maya: creating whitelist now. patch: 
```json
{"whitelist_accounts": ["acme-corp"], "expires_at": 2245001410}
```
apply in 30s.

deploy-bot: Patch applied to canary routing: whitelist acme-corp.

sophie: 429s dropped back to baseline after whitelist. p95 unchanged. no new 5xx.

maya: thanks all. action items: 
- maya: notify customer success and ask customer to smooth bursts or request higher quota
- derek/leon: add a check in deploy playbook to detect account-level quota conflicts during rate canaries
- sophie: continue monitoring p95 and billing token delta for next 30m

derek: also can we add a short-lived dashboard tile for canary vs control p95 and 429 split by account? will help fast decisions.

leon: on it. creating tile now.

oncall-bot: Canary canary-2245 held at 1% due to account quota interaction; whitelist applied for acme-corp. No automated rollback triggered.

maya: closing the thread for now. will open a followup for playbook updates. thanks :thumbsup:
